description:
FILED s519 (Fable, 2026-10-17 23:3x) on the USER's ruling "Go ahead with the round-level cadence, record it in DECIDED. Please evaluate if it helps, in a few sessions."  Ruling: DECIDED ## s519; CLAUDE.md WHAT-TO-RUN-WHEN table (companion column = ROUND; harness row = the PER BATCH exception; the paragraph after the table).

THE CHANGE: the CPAN board tree half (~20 min) and the companion --all --quick (15-25 min, exclusive) are no longer per-batch agent legs.  Fable runs both once per round on the merged main (after every 3-4 merges, or at session end if any merge happened since the last round run), attributes a mover by git bisect over the merge range with one-file runs, edits the row with its cause or hands it to the next brief.  Per batch stays: gate, sweep, corpus-diff + emission-ab + ir-host-leak + ir-conform, everyday + --record, and ONE-FILE acceptance runs of the exact board / companion files a member claims.  Exceptions: a harness change keeps --all --quick per batch; a bounded leg on files the brief NAMES stays.

BASELINE (the per-batch regime, s517-s518, 2026-10-16/17):
  - s518d (4 correctness members): THREE agents -- the first shipped all four members in 28 min and died at ~348k tokens; the second spent its whole context on legs + row-by-row baseline edits (gate, eab, everyday, sweep + re-run, companion + two attribution runs, board) and was cut by session end; a third (s519) only to read the board diff + records.  Legs-only agents per batch: 2.
  - s518e (B shim + census): stopped at ~450k tokens with NO leg run yet (its members + the census + fillers used the budget); its resume runs the legs.
  - s517b: sweep and emission-ab both hit exit 75 (never got the lock in 60 min) behind three exclusive legs; the s518 10:0x / 11:2x slot rules were written because of it.  Fable's own 3-row bench starved s518d's sweep + everyday for ten minutes (s518 11:2x).
  - Wall per batch of the two slow legs: board ~20 min + companion 15-25 min (+ attribution re-runs ~5 min each).

QUESTIONS TO ANSWER AT ~s522 (three sessions of the new regime; read the PAUSE files + session-log for s519-s522):
  1. Agents per batch: how many batches needed a legs-only resume agent?  (baseline: s518d 2 of 3 agents were legs-only)
  2. Tokens: the share of an agent's context spent after its last member commit (legs + attribution) -- from the agents' final reports / STOP.md token notes.
  3. Round runs: how many were run, how long each took Fable, how many movers appeared, and the bisect cost per mover (steps x one-file run time).
  4. Regressions that reached main: any board / companion row that a per-batch leg would have caught before the FF, how many rounds it sat, and whether the fix was a filler or a revert.
  5. Slot waits: exit-75s and > 30-min waits per session (baseline s517b: 2 exit-75s in one morning).
  6. Did any batch's one-file acceptance disagree with the round-level board on the same file (a one-file run passing while the board run fails = an environment / ordering effect worth knowing)?
VERDICT: keep / adjust (e.g. every 2 merges, or per-batch board for dist-targeting batches) / revert -- a one-line DECIDED entry + a CLAUDE.md table edit either way.  Owner: Fable, s522 (or the first session after three rounds).

DATA POINT 1 (s519, 2026-10-17 23:5x, Fable -- recorded BEFORE the new regime applied to this batch): s518d's per-batch board leg (run 12:14 under the OLD regime, its diff read at 23:3x) caught a LOST FILE -- Capture-Tiny t/08-stdin-closed.t 744 -> 1 rows -- caused by #3371's honest fileno(STDIN) = undef making two pre-existing runtime bugs reachable; the agent fixed both as #3372 (commit efdaf775) before MERGE-READY.  Under the round-level cadence this would have reached main and been found at the round run (same session), then bisected to #3371's commit (one-file run of that t-file, ~10 s) -- a one-round exposure, fixed as a filler.  Cost of catching it pre-merge here: a 20-min board leg + the agent re-took gate + sweep (~8 min) on the fix; under the new regime the same fix would need the one-file acceptance only.  Count this under question 4.

DATA POINT 3 (s520, Fable, 2026-10-18 10:2x): the FIRST REGRESSION THAT SAT ON MAIN FOR A ROUND.  s518e's B shim (#3281, merged 01:1x as MAIN-READY-28) made `require B` succeed in op/stash.t / uni/stash.t, so their 29-row B block RUNS and aborts at the shim's designed `B::CV::CvFLAGS` die: 28 + 26 passing rows never produced (op/stash.t 48/7 -> 20/7, uni/stash.t 43/6 -> 17/6).  s518e's bounded companion leg named six op/ files (method universal ref caller symbolcache, mro/overload_c3) -- not stash.t -- and the round-1 companion half was deferred until s519a + s519b merged, so the loss surfaced 8 hours later in s519b's HARNESS-EXCEPTION companion (09:17), i.e. by an exception to the cadence, not by a round run.  Attribution: Fable, two one-file runs (main 02a35add vs the fca3593b base) through heavy.sh, 4 minutes wall, both identical -> #3362 filed; s519b splices the rows with that cause.  Under the per-batch regime s518e's own `--all --quick` would have shown the two files before the FF (cost: ~20 min of an exclusive slot + the agent's attribution).  Question 4's tally so far: data point 1 (s518d, caught per-batch before the FF), data point 3 (s518e, sat one round, caught by the harness exception).  The round-1 companion on the merged main is still owed (after s519b merges) and will re-find these two files.
subject: EVALUATE the round-level test cadence (USER s519: board + companion once per 3-4 merges instead of per batch) at ~s522 -- did it cut agents-per-batch and leg tokens without letting regressions sit on main?
